Therapeutic genome editing promises to transform medicine. Pivotal discoveries have provided a diverse and versatile set of tools to correct pathogenic mutations or produce protective alleles using CRISPR-based technologies. These innovative therapies are especially adaptable for blood and immune disorders, where clinical methods allow hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) to be mobilized, harvested, engineered ex vivo, and transplanted back into a patient to permanently replace their blood system. This paradigm has been exemplified with the first FDA-approved CRISPR-Cas9 therapy for sickle cell disease and β-thalassemia, exa-cel (Casgevy).
